"""tidelog — parse and summarise tide-station log lines."""

from .model import Entry
from .parse import parse_line
from .report import summarise

__all__ = ["Entry", "parse_line", "summarise"]

"""Data model for tidelog entries."""

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class Entry:
    """One log line: timestamp, channel number, and message text."""

    ts: str
    channel: int
    text: str

"""Parse raw tidelog lines into Entry objects."""

from .model import Entry


def parse_line(line: str) -> Entry:
    """Parse a line like `2026-11-02T22:00:00Z | ch 16 | hello harbour`.

    Splits on " | "; the channel field must be "ch <int>".
    Raises ValueError on a malformed line.
    """
    parts = line.rstrip("\n").split(" | ")
    if len(parts) != 3:
        raise ValueError(f"malformed line (expected 3 pipe-separated fields): {line!r}")

    ts, channel_part, text = parts
    channel_str = channel_part[3:] if channel_part.startswith("ch ") else ""
    try:
        channel = int(channel_str)
    except ValueError:
        raise ValueError(f"malformed channel field: {channel_part!r}") from None

    return Entry(ts=ts, channel=channel, text=text)

import pytest

from tidelog import Entry, parse_line


def test_parse_line_good():
    line = "2026-11-02T22:00:00Z | ch 16 | hello harbour"
    entry = parse_line(line)
    assert entry == Entry(ts="2026-11-02T22:00:00Z", channel=16, text="hello harbour")


def test_parse_line_malformed_raises_value_error():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        parse_line("not a tidelog line at all")
